multi-walled carbon nano-tubes (CNTs), when used as plasmid delivery systems, can be successfully employed in bacterial transformation, with the transformation efficiency of E. coli cells being 10 times higher than that of the control group.
multi-walled carbon-nanotubes can be used as plasmid nanocarriers for the efficient transformation of E. coli cells.
multi-walled carbon nanostructures can be used to efficiently deliver plasmids to E. coli cells, and that this delivery method can be used for the transformation of single bacterial cells.

the design of a nanocarrier system for the transformation of E. coli.
the development and application of nanomaterials as tools for biological studies.
the development of a new plasmid delivery method that can be applied to the transformation of bacteria and other cells.

the CNTs have the capability of plasmid delivery and electroporation of bacterial cells.
the results presented here demonstrate a novel method for the efficient and selective delivery of DNA molecules to bacterial cells.
CNTs are a promising tool for plasmid DNA delivery into bacteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CNTs have a high potential for nanoscale plasmid delivery in bacterial cells.
the use of CNTs can significantly reduce the number of cells needed for transformation, while increasing the efficiency of the transformation process.

CNTs can be used as an effective gene delivery vehicle in bacterial cells.
